pages.title: Executive assessment summary
pages.subtitle: From technical findings to business risk and validated remediation.
items: The synthetic environment shows common weaknesses in management-plane protection, network segmentation, privileged access, and security visibility. The principal concern is the combination of broad reachability, privileged exposure, and incomplete monitoring.

A compromised user workstation could create a path toward privileged network control. Excessive east-west access also increases lateral-movement opportunity, while incomplete logging can reduce detection and investigation capability.
The sample shows how weownit.net connects evidence to business impact, remediation ownership, validation criteria, and residual risk - rather than stopping at a list of technical findings.

pages.title: Business context & critical assets
pages.subtitle: Security decisions start with what the organization depends on.
items: ACME Manufacturing is a fictional 250-user organization with a headquarters, two branches, business-critical ERP, internal application services, remote connectivity, and centralized network administration.
Internet edge firewall; management network; ERP and application servers; branch VPN connectivity; centralized security logging; privileged administrative identities.
Protect connectivity availability, integrity of privileged configuration, confidentiality of business data, segmentation between trust zones, and accountability of administrative actions.

pages.title: Scope, assumptions & methodology
pages.subtitle: A repeatable assessment model for risk-informed security engineering.
items: Architecture, trust boundaries, administrative exposure, segmentation, firewall policy, logging, privileged access, configuration backup, and recovery readiness.
CONTEXT -> ASSESS -> ANALYZE -> PRIORITIZE -> REMEDIATE -> VALIDATE -> PROVE
This sample uses SYNTHETIC / INFERRED evidence. In a real engagement, evidence is classified as Observed, Confirmed, Inferred, or Not Tested.

pages.title: Architecture & trust boundaries
pages.subtitle: Where lower-trust zones can reach privileged control.
items: Internet / User / Server / Management / Security Management / Branch VPN

The user network can reach administrative HTTPS/SSH services on the edge firewall. This weakens the trust boundary and creates an unnecessary path from a lower-trust workstation segment to privileged security control.
Administrative access originates only from the management zone or an explicitly approved remote-administration path, protected by MFA, named accounts, least privilege, and centralized audit logging.

pages.title: F-001 - Management plane reachable from the user zone
pages.subtitle: Detailed finding - HIGH / PRIORITY 1
items: Administrative HTTPS and SSH services are reachable from the general corporate user network rather than only through the dedicated management path.

A compromised workstation could establish connectivity to the firewall management plane. Combined with credential compromise or another authentication weakness, this creates a credible path toward privileged control.
Source 10.20.10.25 (USER) -> 10.20.100.1. TCP/443 REACHABLE; TCP/22 REACHABLE. Evidence type: SYNTHETIC.
Unauthorized firewall policy, routing, VPN, or logging changes; service disruption; loss of control integrity.

pages.title: F-001 - Control strategy & validation
pages.subtitle: Prevent, limit, detect, recover - then prove the result.
items: Dedicated management network; approved administrative sources; MFA for privileged access; named administrator accounts.
Role-based administration; least privilege; required management protocols only; VPN/OOB administration where appropriate.
Administrative login logging; failed-authentication monitoring; configuration-change audit trail; centralized security telemetry.
Validated configuration backup; emergency access path; documented rollback procedure; clear recovery ownership.
MEDIUM - restricting management access before confirming alternate administrative connectivity can cause lockout. Verify console/OOB access first.
Approved admin -> HTTPS ALLOW; USER -> HTTPS/SSH BLOCK; Internet -> management BLOCK; MFA REQUIRED; configuration changes LOGGED.
LOW when management sources are restricted, MFA and named accounts are enforced, privileged actions are logged, and negative-path testing is successful.

pages.title: F-002 - Excessive east-west network access
pages.subtitle: Detailed finding - HIGH / PRIORITY 1
items: A broad User-to-Server security policy permits more services than are required for normal business operation.
A compromised workstation can probe or connect to internal services unrelated to the user's business function, increasing the number of reachable targets and potential blast radius.
USER -> APP: required business services only. USER -> DB/MGMT: blocked unless explicitly justified.
Positive test for required application flows plus negative tests for database and management services. Review denied-traffic logs.
MEDIUM after least-privilege policy and monitoring, subject to application dependencies and formally approved exceptions.

pages.title: Remediation roadmap & closure evidence
pages.subtitle: Turn findings into owned, measurable, and verifiable work.
items: Contain privileged exposure: restrict firewall management reachability, verify emergency access, enforce MFA, and assign accountable owners.
Reduce unnecessary trust: replace broad user-to-server access with approved application flows and validate dependencies before enforcement.
Strengthen visibility and recovery: centralize security telemetry, verify audit retention, test configuration restore, and document recovery ownership.
OPEN -> REMEDIATION PLANNED -> IMPLEMENTED -> VALIDATION REQUIRED -> VERIFIED -> CLOSED.
Relevant configuration extract, approved change, positive and negative tests, audit evidence, residual-risk statement, and owner acceptance.
Executive assessment summary + technical findings register + risk-prioritized remediation backlog + architecture observations + validation plan + reusable closure evidence.
